idea: Invoicing and late-payment reminders for freelance designers in the US

strategist.problem: A freelance designer in the US sends invoice #3 for $4,200 to a studio client with Net-15 terms, day 22 passes with no payment, and they are too anxious and busy to send a follow-up email without sounding desperate — cash flow for rent and software subscriptions stalls while they keep doing client work.
strategist.target_customer: Solo freelance graphic/UI designers in the US billing $3k–$12k/month to 3–10 repeat clients on Net-15/Net-30 terms, who feel the pain the moment an invoice passes its due date and they have to chase payment by hand over email.
strategist.mission: Get freelance designers paid on time by turning overdue invoices into automatic, polite-but-firm reminder sequences so they never have to chase a client themselves.

competitors.name: FreshBooks
competitors.differentiator: We win on price and focus: FreshBooks is a full small-business accounting suite at $19+/month, while we only do invoicing plus smart late-payment chasing for solo designers.

competitors.name: Wave
competitors.differentiator: Wave is free but its reminder automation is shallow and its UX targets restaurants and trades; we win with designer-specific invoice templates and escalation logic tied to Net-15/Net-30 terms.

competitors.name: Manual email follow-up in Gmail
competitors.differentiator: We win because the designer never has to draft the awkward 'just checking in' email — our sequence sends, tracks opens, and escalates automatically at day 1, 7, and 14 past due.

scope_cuts: Skipping double-entry accounting, expense tracking, and tax reports — the goal is getting paid, not replacing QuickBooks; those features triple build time and delay revenue.

Skipping Stripe payment processing integration in v1 (invoice links out to PayPal/PayPal.Me or a 'pay by ACH' instruction) — a payments integration requires KYC, compliance review, and would blow the 2–4 week ship window.
Skipping multi-user teams, client portals, and a mobile app — the buyer is a solo freelancer checking overdue invoices on a laptop between design tasks.

stack.name: Next.js (App Router)
stack.why: Full-stack React framework for building the invoice dashboard and reminder logic server-side.

stack.name: Supabase
stack.why: Postgres database with built-in auth and row-level security for managing users, invoices, and reminder states.

stack.name: TailwindCSS + shadcn/ui
stack.why: Rapid UI development for designer-focused, clean invoice templates and dashboard components.

stack.name: Vercel
stack.why: Zero-config hosting for Next.js with commercial usage rights on the Pro plan.

stack.name: Resend
stack.why: Transactional email API to send the automatic, polite-but-firm reminder sequences to clients.

stack.name: Lemon Squeezy
stack.why: Merchant of record for handling global US subscription billing and tax compliance without KYC.

ai_tools.name: Cursor
ai_tools.why: AI code editor to generate Next.js components, Supabase queries, and reminder logic rapidly.

ai_tools.name: v0.dev
ai_tools.why: Generates production-ready React/Tailwind UI for the invoice creation and dashboard screens.

mvp_features: Automatic late-payment reminder sequences (Day 1, 7, 14 past due) with open tracking and polite-but-firm copy.
Designer-specific invoice creation with Net-15/Net-30 terms and PayPal/PayPal.Me payment links.
Dashboard showing overdue invoices, upcoming due dates, and total outstanding balance.
first_10_steps: Run `npx create-next-app@latest invoice-chaser --typescript --tailwind --app` to scaffold the Next.js project.
Run `npx shadcn-ui@latest init` and install `button`, `card`, `input`, `table`, and `dialog` components for the UI.
Create a Supabase project, enable Auth, and write SQL for `users`, `invoices`, and `reminders` tables with RLS policies.
Use Cursor to generate the Supabase client, auth context, and database query functions for invoice CRUD operations.
Use v0.dev to generate the invoice creation form and dashboard table components, then integrate them into the Next.js App Router.
Implement the reminder logic in a Next.js API route that checks invoice due dates and triggers Resend email sequences.
Integrate Lemon Squeezy checkout links for the $19/month subscription and webhook handler to activate user accounts.
Deploy the application to Vercel Pro and connect the Supabase database URL and Resend API key as environment variables.
Test the full flow: create an invoice, mark it overdue, verify the Day 1 reminder email sends via Resend, and track the open.
Manually onboard 5 freelance designers from LinkedIn, provide them with the app URL, and collect feedback on the reminder copy.

pricing.name: Solo
features: Up to 15 active invoices per month
Net-15/Net-30 terms and designer invoice templates

pricing.name: Studio
features: Automatic Day 1/7/14 past-due reminder sequences with open tracking
Custom reminder copy and sender name

revenue_targets.notes: 3 designers converted from ~60 cold LinkedIn/DM outreach touches at ~5% close rate for a no-track-record founder selling $19/mo; avg blended $24 assumes 2 Solo + 1 Studio.
Path from 3 to 14 = 11 new customers via ~200 cumulative outreach touches, 3 referrals from the first 3, and posts in r/freedesign and DesignerNews; avg blended $24.
Break-even crossed at 10 customers; 25 pays for burn 3x over. Avg blended $24.

key_assumptions: Solo US freelance designers billing $3k–$12k/month will pay $19/month to never write a follow-up email themselves — willingness-to-pay rests on a single avoided awkward email per month being worth less than one hour of their $75–$150/hr billing rate.
Blended avg revenue of $24/customer assumes the mix stays roughly 80% Solo ($19) / 20% Studio ($39).

Delivery cost of $3.40/customer/month = Resend free-tier overage headroom ($0.60) + Cloudflare domain amortized ($0.05) + pilot-phase labor: 30 min of founder time per pilot at an implied $75/hr = $37.50, amortized across 15 pilot customers in month 1 = $2.50, plus $0.25 ongoing support credit.
Marketing budget of $150/month is spent on ~60 cold outreach touches plus 1 LinkedIn post boost + 1 IndieHackers/DesignerNews sponsored post; no paid ads beyond that cap.

channels.name: LinkedIn Direct Outreach
channels.tactic: Send 10 templated connection requests/day to US-based freelance graphic/UI designers with 'Freelance' or 'Independent' in title; follow up with 1 DM after acceptance

channels.name: Designer Slack/Discord + Newsletter Outreach
channels.tactic: DM 8 members/day in designer Slack/Discord communities (e.g. Designer Hangout, Freelance Design Hub, ADPList community Slack) with the 3-line message; plus 1 free community-allowed mention/week in designer newsletters like DesignerNews job board or freelance-focused newsletters (1 sponsored slot at $0 free tier or $50 one-off, price not verified)

first_10_customers: Day 1-3: Identify 50 US freelance designers on LinkedIn by filtering for 'Freelance Graphic Designer' + 'United States' + 500-5,000 connections; export list to CSV

Day 4-7: Send 10 templated connection requests/day with note: 'Hi [Name], I'm building a tool that auto-chases overdue invoices for designers. No cost to try — want me to send you a sample reminder sequence for your next Net-30 invoice?'
Day 8-10: DM all accepted connections (target 10-15) with 3-line cold message; offer a 5-minute self-serve pilot: create free account, add one overdue invoice, see the Day 1 reminder scheduled

Day 11-14: DM 8 members/day in Designer Hangout and Freelance Design Hub Slack/Discord channels with the same 3-line message; follow up with 5 non-responders from LinkedIn via email scraped from portfolio sites
Day 15-18: Onboard first 3 pilots through the real app — they create an account, add an overdue invoice, and see the reminder sequence scheduled; collect a 1-sentence testimonial
Day 19-30: Convert pilots to $19/mo Solo tier; ask each for 2 referrals to other designers; repeat outreach to hit 5 paying customers
growth.cold_message: Hi [Name], I'm building a tool that sends polite-but-firm payment reminders for overdue designer invoices — no more awkward 'just checking in' emails. You can set it up in 5 minutes: create an account, add one overdue invoice, and see your Day 1/7/14 reminders scheduled automatically. Want me to send you the link to try it free this week?

objections.objection: I already use FreshBooks/Wave and it's fine
objections.response: Fair — but their reminders are generic and you still have to draft the follow-up. Our tool is built only for designers: it knows Net-15/Net-30 terms, uses designer-specific templates, and escalates automatically at Day 1/7/14. Set up a free account in 5 minutes, add one overdue invoice, and see the sequence scheduled — if it doesn't save you 30+ minutes of awkward email drafting, cancel anytime.

objections.objection: I don't have time to switch tools
objections.response: You don't switch — you layer. Keep your current invoicing tool; we just handle the late-payment chasing. Onboarding takes 5 minutes: create an account, add one overdue invoice, and the Day 1 reminder is scheduled. If it works, you're in for $19/mo; if not, no hard feelings.

critic.verdict: The plan is highly coherent and strictly adheres to the bootstrapped, low-burn constraints, leveraging a lean stack to solve a specific, painful problem for freelance designers. The scope cuts are appropriate for an MVP, and the revenue model is realistic for a solo founder. The primary weakness lies in the operational friction of the payment flow, which may undermine the core value proposition of 'effortless payment chasing.'
critic.biggest_risk: The decision to exclude native payment processing (Stripe/PayPal) in v1 forces designers to manually copy-paste PayPal links or ACH details into invoices, creating a high-friction onboarding step that may cause users to abandon the tool before seeing the value of the automated reminders.
